questions.q: What good habits do you have?
questions.answer: I'd say reading before bed is my best habit. I also keep a to-do list and try to walk most evenings. None of these are dramatic, but together they make my days feel more [[purposeful]].

questions.q: Do you have any habits you would like to change?
questions.answer: One or two, definitely. I spend too long on my phone, and I sometimes [[procrastinate]]. I'm slowly working on both, though old habits are surprisingly hard to break.

questions.q: How do you usually develop a new habit?
questions.answer: I start small and attach it to something I already do. For example, I read ten pages right after my evening tea. Keeping it manageable like that makes a new habit much easier to [[sustain]].

questions.q: Did you have any bad habits as a child?
questions.answer: Oh yes, I used to bite my nails constantly, especially before exams. My mother tried everything to stop me. Eventually I simply [[outgrew]] it, although I still catch myself doing it when I'm nervous.

questions.q: Do you think we learn our habits from our family?
questions.answer: To a large extent, yes. I got my love of tea and my habit of rising early from my parents. Children [[absorb]] a great deal simply by watching the adults around them, both good and bad.
